summary: Revenue management, service automation, and demand forecasting lead adoption - and AI assistants are becoming a discovery channel hotels now compete inside of. Who tracks it: the sector's research firms, its standards and trade bodies, and the platforms actually running pricing and guest operations.

analysis.body:
The official adoption figure comes from Census BTOS, which asks accommodation and food services firms whether they used AI in the last two weeks. The latest reading is 10.1%, up from 8.5% in the prior period. That covers NAICS 72, so it spans hotels, restaurants, and related food-service businesses.

Hotelworld AI's Q1 2026 index tracks 2,105+ hotel brands and 131,000 properties across ChatGPT, Google AI, Perplexity, and Claude, measuring how often hotels appear in AI-generated answers. Its finding is that travellers now ask AI and receive a shortlist rather than scrolling links, making AI visibility the industry's next competitive battleground. Skift Research adds that AI has turned hotel loyalty into a contest on personalization, with no one-size-fits-all strategy. Expedia Group builds generative travel planning and price forecasting, while Amadeus and Sabre apply AI to real-time offer personalization in the global distribution systems.

On the operations side, Canary's guest messaging and check-in AI, Duetto's revenue management, and SevenRooms' guest-experience prediction are where hospitality AI reaches daily operations. Canary reports it is trusted by 20,000+ hotels worldwide and natively integrates with major property management systems, CRMs, and payment providers. In food service, Yum Brands deploys voice ordering and kitchen computer vision across its chains, with SoundHound and ConverseNow as the conversational-AI vendors taking orders. The National Restaurant Association tracks AI drive-thru, kitchen robotics, and predictive ordering across restaurant and QSR chains.

The industry bodies concentrate on standards and deployment recognition rather than AI-specific regulation. AHLA, which absorbed the HTNG technology standards body, is where hotel-systems interoperability and AI deployment recognition live. HFTP hosts HITEC, the sector's largest technology exposition, and tracks AI deployment research in lodging. The excerpts do not surface a specific regulatory posture for AI in hospitality; the National Restaurant Association's materials focus on operational risk guides like public safety and utility disruptions, not AI rules.

For a reader deciding whether to deploy, the measured adoption is still modest at 10.1%, but the direction is upward from 8.5%. The sources report qualitative benefits, such as Canary's claim that its software improves guest experience, streamlines operations, and boosts revenue, but no measured ROI percentages appear in these excerpts. The clearest takeaway is that AI is already reshaping discovery and personalization, and hotels that ignore AI-generated shortlists risk losing visibility, while operators should choose paths suited to their specific needs rather than expecting one standard approach.

https://www.ahla.com/.brief: AHLA supports the hotel industry through advocacy, resources, and initiatives that strengthen businesses and the workforce. It runs a voluntary, bipartisan Political Action Committee that helps elect federal candidates who back lodging. The association offers industry-wide connections, events, discounts, updates, and a state-by-state economic impact dashboard, as well as an Allied Attorney Directory. AHLA also pushes legislation on sustainability, workforce development, and human trafficking prevention, and provides policy talking points and best-practice guides. Its membership includes brand companies, owners, management firms, independents, suppliers, and state lodging associations, giving unified advocacy on Capitol Hill and local levels.

https://www.hftp.org/.brief: HFTP describes itself as an international nonprofit association with more than 70 years of history supporting hospitality professionals through education, events, networking, research, and skill-building programs. The organization reports 83 chapters worldwide, including locations in the United States, Canada, Mexico, the Caribbean, the United Arab Emirates, and India. A statement from HFTP Global President James Bina says the association continues to “address changing business practices and provide information to help you navigate them.” The page also notes a strategic partnership between the Hospitality Tech EXPO and HITEC for a first HITEC TOKYO event, a Mid-South Atlantic Regional Conference, and resources such as Hotel Online, Clubs Online, and the Corporate Allied Sponsors program.

https://restaurant.org/.brief: The National Restaurant Association describes its work helping members build customer loyalty, achieve financial success, and provide foodservice careers. The page highlights free resources, including a guide for reducing risk and responding to public safety incidents and a guide for preparing for and recovering from utility outages. It also promotes the Kids LiveWell program for offering meal options that meet nutrition criteria. Upcoming webinars cover foodborne illness prevention with Ecolab experts, high-performing beverage categories, and career skills developed in the restaurant industry. The association notes that the industry is the nation’s second-largest private sector employer.

https://research.skift.com/.brief: Skift Research reports that artificial intelligence has turned hotel loyalty into a contest centered on personalization, but no single strategy fits every hotel. The page describes its content as global travel industry intelligence with news, information, data, and analysis on airlines, hotels, tourism, cruises, startups, and technology. It states that hotels must decide which personalization path best suits their needs.

https://www.expediagroup.com/.brief: The Expedia Group homepage presents the company as a travel marketplace that connects travelers, partners, and experiences through trusted brands and technology. It says the marketplace offers hotels, vacation rentals, packages, flights, and more, giving travelers many ways to plan and book. The page says, “Expedia Group isn’t just a travel marketplace ,  we’re a catalyst for positive change,” and claims the company aims to create a smarter, more sustainable travel future. It also notes that partners use its B2B technology and advertising solutions to deliver exceptional experiences, and that the company is recognized as a top workplace.
